product.name: ZCode

pricing.value: no separate ZCode seat on opened pages; GLM Coding Plan prices

notFor: idle-time is not for Start Plan or API-key mode

sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `zcode`
- Canonical name: ZCode (`claim-zcode-sf-identity`)
- Vendor: Z.AI (`claim-zcode-sf-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: https://zcode.z.ai/en (`claim-zcode-sf-canonical-url`)
- Public repository: unknown (`claim-zcode-sf-repository-url`)
- Current status: public desktop app labelled v3.7.7 (`claim-zcode-sf-status`, `claim-zcode-sf-version`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15
- Distinct from `zai-coding-plugins` (`claim-zcode-sf-not-plugins`)
- GLM Coding Plan is a model subscription, not this product (`claim-zcode-sf-not-coding-plan`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: Z.AI's first-party Agentic Development Environment and official harness for GLM-5.3 (`claim-zcode-sf-what-it-is`, `claim-zcode-sf-identity`, `claim-zcode-sf-primary-type`)
- What it is not: not the Claude Code plugin marketplace at `zai-org/zai-coding-plugins` (`claim-zcode-sf-not-plugins`); not the GLM Coding Plan itself (`claim-zcode-sf-not-coding-plan`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `ide` from first-party ADE wording (`claim-zcode-sf-primary-type`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-ide`)
- Agent-loop owner: official docs name ZCode Agent as the default self-developed agent that organizes tasks, permissions, context, tool calls, and review (`claim-zcode-sf-agent-loop`). That is vendor wording, not a hands-on loop-owner proof
- Architecture: desktop ADE client; in a remote workspace the Agent, files, terminal, and Git run on the target host, WSL distribution, or container while account and model settings stay on the desktop (`claim-zcode-sf-architecture`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-zcode-desktop`, `surface-zcode-mobile-remote`, `surface-zcode-wechat`, `surface-zcode-feishu`, `surface-zcode-telegram`, `surface-zcode-remote-ssh`
- Execution location: same-device for local workspaces (`claim-zcode-sf-execution-local`); SSH remote host (`claim-zcode-sf-execution-ssh`); WSL on Windows (`claim-zcode-sf-execution-wsl`); local Docker container (`claim-zcode-sf-execution-docker`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: GLM-5.3-first with selectable other models, thought levels, and Coding Plan versus API-key modes (`claim-zcode-sf-model-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: Continue with Z.ai, Continue with BigModel, or Use API Key (`claim-zcode-sf-auth-strategy`)
- Provider support: Z.ai, BigModel, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Moonshot, OpenAI, MiniMax, Xiaomi MiMo, and custom Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`claim-zcode-sf-provider-support`)
- Subscription reuse: a bound GLM Coding Plan supplies quota (`claim-zcode-sf-subscription-reuse`)
- BYOK: API-key providers (`claim-zcode-sf-byok`)
- First-party local-model runtime: unknown (`claim-zcode-sf-model-strategy`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: official 1M GLM-5.3 context on the welcome page (`claim-zcode-sf-context`); Coding Plan / Start Plan windows are server-issued and `[1m]` models are fixed at 1M on the configuration page (`claim-zcode-sf-context-windows`)
- Memory: handwritten `AGENTS.md` (`claim-zcode-sf-agents-md`); optional project Memory off by default, local files only, not on remotes (`claim-zcode-sf-memory`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-persistent-memory`, `claim-zcode-sf-data-path-memory`). Memory docs still say no in-app management page (`claim-zcode-sf-memory-no-ui`); changelog 3.7.5 says Settings can browse project memories (`claim-zcode-sf-memory-settings-browse`). Keep both.
- Compaction: automatic before the window is full; no user threshold (`claim-zcode-sf-compaction`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-compaction`). Command docs also list `/compact` (`claim-zcode-sf-compact-command`)
- Session behavior: durable desktop tasks, fork from a completed assistant message, temporary desktop-only side conversations (`claim-zcode-sf-session`, `claim-zcode-sf-session-fork`). Remote Control continues an already-open desktop window (`claim-zcode-sf-session-remote-control`). WeChat / Feishu bots continue the desktop workspace task (`claim-zcode-sf-session-bot`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: workspace files, built-in browser, terminal, find/grep, and background commands (`claim-zcode-sf-tools`). Custom-subagent checkboxes name Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write, WebFetch, WebSearch, and TodoWrite (`claim-zcode-sf-tools-names`)
- Extensions: first-party plugin store, official built-ins, and a preloaded Claude Code marketplace (`claim-zcode-sf-extensions`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-plugins`)
- MCP: stdio, HTTP, and SSE client with user/workspace/plugin sources (`claim-zcode-sf-mcp`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-mcp`)
- Skills: `SKILL.md` via `$` or the slash Skills group; no standalone skill marketplace (`claim-zcode-sf-skills`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-skills`)
- Hooks: user and plugin hooks; project-level hooks ignored (`claim-zcode-sf-hooks`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-hooks`)
- APIs: unknown (`claim-zcode-sf-api`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: ZCode Agent plus built-in general-purpose and Explore subagents and beta custom subagents (`claim-zcode-sf-orchestration`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-subagents`). Goal Mode `/goal` is a separate page (`claim-zcode-sf-orchestration-goal`)
- Parallelism: parallel foreground subagents; optional background subagents; no nested subagents (`claim-zcode-sf-parallelism`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: unknown as a default local OS sandbox (`claim-zcode-sf-isolation`)
- Permissions: Confirm Before Changes is the default execution mode (`claim-zcode-sf-permissions`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-permissions`)
- Security: Remote Control links are temporary keys (`claim-zcode-sf-security`); enabled plugins can run local processes (`claim-zcode-sf-security-plugins`); hooks execute local code (`claim-zcode-sf-security-hooks`); MCP secrets copy as-is on remote sync (`claim-zcode-sf-security-mcp-secrets`)
- Data path: inference goes to the connected provider; HTTP proxy scope excludes sign-in, Wiki, Web Remote Control, and SSH (`claim-zcode-sf-data-path`). Memory files stay local and the Memory page says nothing is uploaded for that feature (`claim-zcode-sf-data-path-memory`)

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
Keep desktop, Mobile Remote, WeChat, Feishu, and Telegram distinct. Do not collapse them.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Desktop ADE: `surface-zcode-desktop` (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-desktop`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-desktop`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-local-execution`)
  - Mobile Remote Control (phone browser): `surface-zcode-mobile-remote` (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-mobile-remote`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-mobile-web`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-remote-control`)
  - WeChat Bot Channel: `surface-zcode-wechat` (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-wechat`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-messaging`)
  - Feishu Bot Channel: `surface-zcode-feishu` (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-feishu`)
  - Telegram: `surface-zcode-telegram` — homepage names it (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-telegram-homepage`); Bot Channel docs do not list it as available (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-telegram-docs`)
  - SSH remote development: `surface-zcode-remote-ssh` (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-ssh`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-remote-machine`)
- Remote behavior: remote development chooses where code runs; Remote Control and Bot Channel drive a desktop session from away (`claim-zcode-sf-access-routes-split`, `claim-zcode-sf-remote-access`). ADE Tools currently names SSH and Docker (`claim-zcode-sf-ade-tools-remote-kinds`); Remote Development also names WSL on Windows (`claim-zcode-sf-execution-wsl`). Keep both.
- Mobile behavior: phone-browser QR/link Remote Control (`claim-zcode-sf-mobile-access`); WeChat/Feishu bots (`claim-zcode-sf-mobile-access-bots`); welcome claims desktop parity for Mobile Remote (`claim-zcode-sf-mobile-access-parity`); side conversation entry hidden on mobile (`claim-zcode-sf-mobile-access-side`). No native store app established
- Background behavior: idle-time local queue (`claim-zcode-sf-background`); scheduled automations (`claim-zcode-sf-scheduled`); Windows close-to-tray (`claim-zcode-sf-background-tray`); background terminal (`claim-zcode-sf-background-terminal`, `claim-zcode-sf-tag-background`). Idle-time docs deny background subagents in that mode.
- Native iOS / native Android / Termux / generic remote shell: unknown (`claim-zcode-sf-mobile-access`)
- First-party CLI: unknown (`claim-zcode-sf-availability`). Changelog 3.7.6 names headless sessions but does not say how to start one (`claim-zcode-sf-headless-changelog`)

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: opened ZCode pages do not sell a separate ZCode seat; homepage Lite/Pro/Max cards are GLM Coding Plan prices with final details on z.ai (`claim-zcode-sf-pricing`). 5-day trial and subscriber idle-time free runs (`claim-zcode-sf-pricing-trial`)
- License: unknown (`claim-zcode-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: changelog through v3.7.7 on 2026-08-14 (`claim-zcode-sf-maintenance`)
- Lock-in / positioning: welcome exclusive-benefits / Coding Plan CTA (`claim-zcode-sf-lock-in`); homepage official-harness (`claim-zcode-sf-lock-in-official`); configuration recommends Z.ai Coding Plan for global users and still lists third-party providers (`claim-zcode-sf-lock-in-providers`)
- Availability: homepage macOS, Windows, Linux x64/ARM64 `.deb` and AppImage; Linux labelled Beta (`claim-zcode-sf-availability`). Install page says Linux (x64, AppImage) only (`claim-zcode-sf-availability-install`). Keep both. Do not average.

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: plugin page has `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` fallback and a preloaded Claude Code marketplace (`claim-zcode-sf-lineage`); hook I/O includes Claude Code snake_case aliases (`claim-zcode-sf-lineage-hooks`); `CLAUDE.md` is a one-time migration source (`claim-zcode-sf-agents-md`). This is not an official `fork_of` or `wraps_cli` claim
- Relationship edges: none. Isolated pack has only `zcode`. No evidenced directed edge to another project id

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: unknown
- Substitutes: unknown
- Partial substitutes: unknown
- Same-lineage relatives: unknown
- Often-confused products: `zai-coding-plugins` is a different product (Claude Code marketplace) (`claim-zcode-sf-not-plugins`). That is identity, not a neighborhood membership
- Complements: unknown

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: homepage official-harness plus Bot control (`claim-zcode-sf-unique`); welcome ADE around ZCode Agent with desktop, Remote, and Bot Channel (`claim-zcode-sf-unique-welcome`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: automations are local-desktop-only (`claim-zcode-sf-drawback`); Memory off by default and remote-unsupported (`claim-zcode-sf-drawback-memory`); project hooks ignored (`claim-zcode-sf-drawback-hooks`); Telegram docs conflict with the homepage (`claim-zcode-sf-surface-telegram-docs`)
- Best fit: developers who want a first-party GLM-5.3 desktop ADE (`claim-zcode-sf-intended-user`). This is not a recommendation
- Not-for: installing Z.ai plugins into Claude Code (`claim-zcode-sf-not-plugins`); idle-time tasks on Start Plan or plain API-key mode (`claim-zcode-sf-not-for`)

claims.claim: The last user message can be edited and resent so the agent continues from the corrected instruction; editing is unavailable while a task is running or messages are queued, and only user messages of the latest turn can be edited.
claims.value: {"scope":"latest turn, user messages only","blocked_when":["task running","messages queued"]}
claims.notes: Distinct from the canonical fork behavior, which starts a new task from a completed assistant message.

claims.claim: The home page now bills ZCode as the Official Harness for GLM-5.3 taking multi-agent development further, with the strapline Simple, Fast, Vibe-Ready.
claims.value: official GLM-5.3 harness pushing multi-agent development
claims.notes: Marketing wording changed since the canonical capture; the official-harness positioning is unchanged.

claims.claim: Under WSLg, ZCode and the browser must be launched from the same WSL or Linux environment for browser login to return to the app.
claims.value: same WSL/Linux environment for app and browser
claims.notes: A practical constraint on the canonical browser-account login path.

claims.claim: Linux and WSLg guidance says to run as a regular user, install either the deb package or the AppImage but not both, keep the AppImage at a fixed path, and install libfuse2 when only FUSE 3 is present.
claims.value: {"packages":["deb","AppImage"],"conflict":"installing both can break the system URL handler","dependency":"libfuse2 for AppImage on FUSE-3-only distributions"}
claims.notes: Names a deb package that the canonical install claim did not record, and confirms WSLg as a supported desktop host.

claims.claim: A repository wiki reads through the codebase and generates a per-workspace architecture guide whose claims each carry a clickable source location.
claims.value: {"scope":"one wiki per workspace","content":"architecture guide, not user documentation","settings":["language","model","diagrams","retries"]}
claims.notes: Canonical had no repository knowledge-base claim.

claims.claim: Generating the wiki sends code context, filtered by ZCode's safety rules and read on demand, to the selected model service, and stores the result in the runtime environment of the current workspace.
claims.value: {"sends":"filtered code context to the selected model service","stores":"workspace runtime environment"}
claims.notes: The page's language is safety-filtered code context read on demand and sent to the selected model service; it does not say the whole repository is sent. No comparison with the Memory feature is established by this page.

claims.claim: The wiki entry is hidden while a remote workspace is disconnected or the workspace is read-only.
claims.value: hidden for disconnected remote or read-only workspaces
claims.notes: Matches the canonical pattern of local-first features with weaker remote coverage.

claims.claim: A permission request pauses the task, blocks the composer, and offers Allow, Always Allow, Reject, and Always Reject; requests are scoped to the task and survive switching away.
claims.value: {"decisions":["Allow","Always Allow","Reject","Always Reject"],"pending_behavior":"task pauses, composer blocked, request persists"}
claims.notes: Gives the approve-actions detail that the canonical surface rows left unstated.

claims.claim: App Usage reads local ZCode session records on the current device and reports tokens, sessions, messages, active days, streaks, peak hour, daily trends, an activity heatmap, and a model ranking.
claims.value: {"scope":"local session records on the current device","ranges":["All Time","Last 30 Days","Last 7 Days"]}
claims.notes: Device-scoped, not an account-wide history.

claims.claim: The Coding Plan view reads remote Z.ai or BigModel statistics and shows a 5-hour prompt pool, weekly quota, monthly MCP quota, per-model token consumption, and tool-call usage.
claims.value: {"quota_pools":["5-hour prompt pool","weekly quota","monthly MCP quota"],"sources":["Z.ai Coding Plan","BigModel Coding Plan"]}
claims.notes: First first-party evidence of the quota shape behind the Coding Plan. No currency amounts are given.

claims.claim: ADE Tools and Bot Channel docs split routes: remote development chooses where code runs; Remote Control and Bot Channel are away-from-desk entry points that drive a session already on the desktop.
claims.value: remote development vs Remote Control vs Bot Channel

claims.claim: ADE Tools says remote development currently shows SSH remote host and Docker local container options.
claims.value: ADE Tools lists SSH and Docker

claims.claim: Official docs say ZCode Agent is the default self-developed agent and that tasks, permissions, context, tool calls, and review flow are organized around it.
claims.notes: Vendor wording, not a hands-on loop-owner verification. Do not treat this as wraps_cli evidence.

claims.claim: ZCode reads ~/.zcode/AGENTS.md and the current workspace AGENTS.md. It does not merge nested AGENTS.md files. CLAUDE.md is used only as a one-time onboarding migration source into AGENTS.md.
Opened first-party pages did not establish a public ZCode product SDK or HTTP API as a user-facing surface.
claims.notes: Absence on opened pages is not proof that no API exists.

claims.claim: The desktop client is the ADE surface. In a remote workspace, file reads, terminal, Git, and Agent execution happen in the target host, WSL distribution, or container; account, model config, and UI stay on the desktop client.
claims.value: desktop ADE; remote workspaces execute on the target

claims.claim: First launch can Continue with Z.ai, Continue with BigModel, or Use API Key. Coding Plan authorization binds the account; API Key mode uses provider keys and coding or general endpoints.
claims.value: Z.ai or BigModel account, or API key

claims.claim: Desktop installers exist for macOS Apple Silicon and Intel, Windows x64 and ARM64, and Linux x64/ARM64 .deb and AppImage. Homepage labels Linux as Beta.
claims.value: macOS, Windows, Linux desktop; Linux beta
claims.notes: Install-page narrower Linux line is claim-zcode-sf-availability-install. Keep both. Do not average. No first-party CLI installer was established on opened pages.

claims.claim: The install page says it supports macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel), Windows (x64 / ARM64), and Linux (x64, AppImage). The download row offered on that page is Linux x64 AppImage only.
claims.value: install page Linux x64 AppImage only
claims.notes: Contradiction with homepage Linux x64/ARM64 .deb and AppImage (claim-zcode-sf-availability). Keep both. Do not average. Whether the install line overrides the homepage list is unknown.

claims.claim: Idle-time tasks join a spare-capacity queue and run on the local machine. The computer must stay awake. Desktop and local projects only; remote workspaces are not supported, and automations do not appear in the mobile remote control interface. The page names scheduled tasks as the similar local-awake case. This page also says background subagents are not supported inside idle-time.
claims.value: local idle-time queue; machine must stay awake; no idle-time background subagents
claims.notes: Idle-time is rolling out to subscribers. Windows tray is claim-zcode-sf-background-tray. Background terminal is claim-zcode-sf-background-terminal. Background subagents outside idle-time are claim-zcode-sf-parallelism.

claims.claim: ADE Tools says the Agent can push long-running terminal commands to the background so the current turn does not wait.
